summary: This review unifies superconducting circuits (SCs) as multi-purpose quantum laboratories spanning condensed matter physics, dark matter detection, and quantum information science. SCs leverage their high-quality microwave resonators and coherent control capabilities to simultaneously serve as precision measurement instruments for discovering emergent quantum phenomena and as platforms for generating and manipulating quantum resources like entanglement and magic.
motivation: Superconducting circuits have historically enabled precision metrology and quantum measurements before modern quantum computing, but recent advances in coherence times and control have positioned them as general-purpose discovery tools across multiple scientific domains.
method: The review traces the technical evolution of SC platforms including circuit-QED and waveguide-QED architectures, describes their use as high-sensitivity resonant probes for condensed matter systems through frequency and linewidth shifts, details quantum-enhanced dark matter detection schemes using transmon single-photon counters and squeezed states, and discusses hardware-native generation of entanglement and non-local magic through engineered nonlinear interactions and AI-assisted optimization.
result: Recent experiments achieved single-photon dark matter sensitivities of $10^{-22}$–$3 \times 10^{-23}$ W/Hz and dark count rates of $\sim 0.1$ s$^{-1}$; SC-based spectroscopy extracted kinetic inductances up to $1.2$ nH/□ in NbSe$_2$ monolayers and resolved nodal superconductivity in twisted graphene through power-law temperature scaling; neural-network design workflows achieved $<2\%$ errors with $\sim 2000\times$ speedup in qubit parameter prediction.
